title: Provision and Rivergate
premise: Oscar Yarrow, a bush pilot who ferries medicine and gossip along the Rivergate and lands wherever the fog allows, pulls a sealed chest from a flooded channel and finds it stamped with the seal of Vessany, a nation erased from the maps forty years ago. Inside are documents proving the Provision—a famine-relief fund that built half the river towns—was looted by the families who now govern the interior, including the magistrate who once saved Oscar's life. Hunted by the magistrate's enforcer, stranded by the monsoon, and forced downriver in a leaking boat with a stranger named Ilse who has her own claim to the chest, Oscar must decide whether truth is worth the family they never had. The story ends with Oscar testifying at the Provision hearings in Rivergate, choosing to stay—grounded, exposed, and finally home—even as the magistrate walks free and Ilse disappears upriver with half the proof.
about_author: Odile Whitlock is the pen name of a former river-freight dispatcher who spent a decade mapping backwater airstrips for a regional relief outfit before turning to fiction. She writes from a houseboat that winters in dry dock, and claims she has never once landed a plane.

chapters.title: Fog Ledger
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A routine medicine run through fog establishes Oscar's rules: never land twice in the same place, never learn names too well, never carry anything but cargo. The emotional beat is the loneliness of a life built on departures.

chapters.title: The River Gives Up a Secret
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. After a storm, Oscar spots a chest snagged in a flooded channel and hauls it aboard, half out of salvage habit. The Vessany seal stops them cold. The beat is curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What Vessany Was
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, introduced as a passenger Oscar reluctantly agrees to ferry. She recognizes the seal instantly and lies badly about why. The beat is two liars circling each other over shared cargo.

chapters.title: Medicine and Rumors
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At a river town, Oscar hears the chest already has a price on it—someone paid for word of its recovery. Oscar pretends ignorance. The beat is the first taste of being hunted.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Debt
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV in flashback and present. We learn Magistrate Corven once pulled Oscar from a wreck and gave them their first job. A summons arrives from Corven himself. The beat is loyalty's gravity.

chapters.title: Ilse's Half of the Story
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She reveals her grandmother was a Vessany clerk who smuggled out the fund's ledgers; Ilse has spent years tracking the chest. The beat is reluctant trust.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Corven's men sabotage the plane at a fuel stop. Oscar realizes the magistrate wants the chest quietly, not legally. The beat is the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. With the plane dead and the monsoon arriving, Oscar and Ilse buy a rotten riverboat from a one-eyed trader named Brannoch. The beat is grim humor in a bad bargain.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rules
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The first storm nearly swamps them; they learn the boat, the river, and each other's limits. The beat is forced intimacy.

chapters.title: The Chest Opens
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They finally crack the chest: ledgers, correspondence, and a list of names—the Provision's architects and its thieves. Corven's signature is on the worst page. The beat is betrayal.

chapters.title: Brannoch's Price
chapters.summary: Brannoch's POV. The old trader knows what they carry and offers to run them downriver anyway—for a share and a promise. The beat is found family's first, wary seed.

chapters.title: Enforcer
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Corven's enforcer, Sable, boards them at a checkpoint and lets them go—too easily. Oscar understands they're being followed, not stopped. The beat is paranoia.

chapters.title: The Town That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. In a village built with Provision money, an old woman recognizes the ledger names and weeps. The beat is the human weight of the theft.

chapters.title: Corven's Letter
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A letter from Corven reaches them via pilot friend: return the chest, and the past stays buried; Oscar's old debts vanish. The beat is temptation with a familiar face.

chapters.title: Sable's Wreck
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They find Sable's patrol boat wrecked—not by accident. Someone else wants the chest, someone who isn't Corven. The beat is a widening conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Third Party
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. A river cartel that laundered the stolen Provision money has hired its own hunters. Ilse admits the chest makes them all targets. The beat is the noose tightening.

chapters.title: Bailout
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The boat's bilge pump dies in open water; Oscar and Brannoch bail by hand through the night while Ilse navigates blind. The beat is solidarity forged in exhaustion.

chapters.title: Names We Don't Say
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Around a driftwood fire, the three trade the histories that made them run—Oscar's, at last, half-told. The beat is found family becoming real.

chapters.title: The Pilot's Grave
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They pass the channel where Oscar's mentor died flying the same routes. Oscar admits why they never stop moving. The beat is grief surfacing.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Two Sisters
chapters.summary: Brannoch's POV. A cartel checkpoint demands the chest; Brannoch bluffs with forged papers and a bottle of terrible brandy. The beat is nerve over firepower.

chapters.title: Sable Again
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Sable, half-drowned, is pulled from the river. She owes them a life and offers a warning instead of a bullet: Corven plans to burn Rivergate's records before the hearings. The beat is an enemy turned uneasy mirror.

chapters.title: The Copy
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse reveals she's been transcribing the ledgers nightly; the chest is bait now, the copies the real cargo. The beat is cunning as survival.

chapters.title: What Corven Built
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A stop at Corven's home district shows schools and clinics the stolen money actually built—and the families it starved. The beat is the corruption's terrible ambiguity.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Fuel Dock
chapters.summary: Brannoch's POV. Brannoch's old debts catch up; he's forced to signal their position to the cartel. The beat is loyalty cracking under old chains.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The cartel attacks at night; the boat burns; the chest goes overboard. Brannoch takes a bullet getting Ilse clear. The beat is sacrifice.

chapters.title: Salvage
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. They recover the chest from the shallows and haul the wounded Brannoch to a mission clinic. The beat is tending what's broken—boat, man, trust.

chapters.title: Brannoch's Confession
chapters.summary: Brannoch's POV. From the clinic cot, Brannoch admits the signal and asks nothing. Oscar chooses to forgive. The beat is found family surviving betrayal.

chapters.title: Corven in Person
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Corven meets them on the river, alone, and makes his final offer: silence, wealth, and the mentor's memory restored. Oscar refuses. The beat is loyalty to truth over loyalty to a savior.

chapters.title: Sable's Choice
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ordered to kill them, Sable instead gives Corven's route schedule to Rivergate and vanishes. The beat is an enforcer defecting.

chapters.title: The Last Rapids
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The final run to Rivergate through monsoon rapids in a patched boat; Brannoch navigates from memory, half-healed. The beat is terror and resolve.

chapters.title: Rivergate
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. They reach the city under curfew, records already burning in the magistrate's annex. The beat is arrival at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Burning Annex
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They raid the annex fire line to save what records remain; Oscar nearly dies pulling out the master register. The beat is courage with cost.

chapters.title: Hearings
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The Provision hearings open; Ilse testifies with her grandmother's transcriptions. The beat is a lifetime of hiding spent in one public hour.

chapters.title: Oscar on the Stand
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar testifies to the chest, the offers, the sabotage—naming Corven. The beat is choosing exposure over invisibility.

chapters.title: The Verdict That Isn't
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Corven walks on procedural grounds; the fund's theft is confirmed, the families implicated. Justice is partial. The beat is bitter, honest resolution.

chapters.title: What Stays
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse decides to carry copies upriver to the erased villages; the chest goes to a river museum, open to all. The beat is letting go.

chapters.title: The Hangar
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar repairs the plane with Brannoch's help but doesn't fly out. For the first time, staying is a choice, not a failure. The beat is quiet homecoming.

chapters.title: A Wake on the Water
chapters.summary: Brannoch's POV. The three hold a wake for the boat, the dead, and the old lives, with the whole river town turning out. The beat is found family made public.

chapters.title: Upriver
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Months later, Oscar flies supply runs again—but now with a home field, a name on the hangar, and letters waiting. The beat is movement with an anchor.

chapters.title: The Chest's Last Secret
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, closing. A letter arrives from upriver in Ilse's hand: one ledger page was withheld, naming Oscar's own mentor among the clerks who hid the money. Oscar reads it twice, folds it away, and chooses to keep flying anyway. The beat is truth and loyalty finally at peace—imperfectly, permanently.
